title: feat(spec): declare the mobile sign-in hand-off surface (one-time-token hand-off and verify, registered app schemes)
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-warren"} -->
_Requested by **Warren** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01U5RdnAAmkSQmZbqh6FtqZ8?thread=cmsg_01U5RdnAAmkSQmZbqh6FtqZ8PKyTDyCuaiBJ67xQB1FoTM)_
Fixes #29736

Clause-②: yes
Metadata-protocol: added
Skills-docs: none — no file under `skills/**` or the hand-written docs teaches `trustedOrigins`, the auth endpoint paths or a mobile sign-in, so nothing taught becomes false and there is no page the new key belongs on yet; the generated reference pages (`content/docs/references/api/auth-endpoints.mdx`, `system/auth-config.mdx`) carry it.

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么:在 `packages/spec` 声明移动端登录交接的契约:两条路由(`/one-time-token/handoff` 与 better-auth 自带的 `/one-time-token/verify`)及其请求/响应 schema,和新的可编写键 `AuthConfig.trustedAppSchemes`(允许回跳的原生 App scheme 列表)。
- 为什么改:部分身份提供方(如 Google)拒绝内嵌 WebView,移动端要走系统浏览器登录再把会话交回 WebView;契约先行,服务端卡 #29714 等本卡落地才转 ready。
- 风险与回滚:只加不减(新键可选、新导出),既有配置零变化;回滚即 revert 本 PR。最敏感处是 scheme 校验规则写严了(必须小写、含点、不带 `://`),错写的条目会被拒而不是被修正。
- 先看:`packages/spec/src/system/auth-config.zod.ts`(`TrustedAppSchemeSchema` 正则与 `trustedAppSchemes` 文档块)、`packages/spec/src/api/auth-endpoints.zod.ts`(交接 query 与 verify 绑定方式)、`.changeset/29736-mobile-sign-in-handoff-spec.md`。
- 两分钟验证:`pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec exec vitest run src/system/auth-config.test.ts src/api/auth-endpoints.test.ts`,预期全部通过,其中 `myapp`、`https`、`com.example.app://` 三种写法都被拒。
- 需要你做的:无,席位落地。

## What changes

The spec half of the mobile sign-in hand-off. The server half is the #29714 card (draft until this lands). The shapes below were agreed with that card's thread before writing. They were built against better-auth 1.7.12, the version `plugin-auth` pins, and measured from its `dist/plugins/one-time-token`.

- **`AuthEndpointPaths.oneTimeTokenHandoff`** = `/one-time-token/handoff` (GET, ObjectStack's own route) with **`OneTimeTokenHandoffQuerySchema`**. It is a strict, closed set:
  - `redirect_uri`;
  - `code_challenge`, an RFC 7636 S256 challenge (43 base64url characters);
  - `code_challenge_method`, optional, only `S256`.

  The docblock states the answers. On success, a `302` to `redirect_uri` with a `token` query parameter, `no-store`, valid for one minute. A `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` with no redirect for an unknown or repeated parameter, an unregistered scheme or a bad challenge. A `401` without a session.
- **`AuthEndpointPaths.oneTimeTokenVerify`** = `/one-time-token/verify` (POST, better-auth's route name and body) with **`OneTimeTokenVerifyRequestSchema`** and **`OneTimeTokenVerifyResponseSchema`**.
  - The interception binding rides inside better-auth's own `token` field: the token, a dot, then the RFC 7636 verifier. The stock client keeps working, and a callback intercepted by another app cannot be redeemed without the verifier. The vendor token alphabet (`a-z A-Z 0-9 - _`, measured from `generateRandomString`) never contains a dot, so the server splits on the first one.
  - The response is better-auth's unwrapped `{ session, user }`, reusing `SessionSchema` / `SessionUserSchema` from `api/auth.zod.ts`.
  - better-auth's `GET /one-time-token/generate` is mounted but refuses client requests (`disableClientRequest`), so it is deliberately not declared.
- **`AuthConfig.trustedAppSchemes`**: a new authorable key, an optional array of **`TrustedAppSchemeSchema`**. The rule is strict and never normalised: a lowercase RFC 3986 scheme written bare, with at least one dot. RFC 8252 section 7.1 requires a private-use scheme to be a reverse domain name. That requirement also rules out, by construction, every web scheme (`http`, `https`, `ws`, `wss`, `javascript`, `data`, `file`, `blob`, `about`, `vbscript`), because none of them contains a dot. A bad entry is refused, never dropped. The docblock states that a hand-off to an unregistered scheme is refused with `400` and no redirect. The server half refuses the same entries at boot, since `plugin-auth` receives plain objects.
- **No `/auth/config` feature flag.** Nothing in the tree reads one. `PUBLIC_AUTH_FEATURES` precedent (passkeys withdrawn) says not to advertise ahead of a consumer, so `kernel/public-auth-features.ts` is untouched.
- Regenerated: `api-surface/`, `export-origins/`, `declaration-map/`, `authorable-surface/`, `json-schema.manifest/`, the strictness-ledger counts and two reference pages. Three isomorphic alias pins were added (ADR-0122), 819 → 822.

**Key-name precedent (the seat's call under the veto window):** `trustedAppSchemes` sits beside `trustedOrigins` on `AuthConfigSchema` and follows its `trusted…` + plural-noun form. It is a separate key on purpose. better-auth trusts an origin in `trustedOrigins` for every redirect it makes, while a scheme here is trusted only as the hand-off's destination. The query parameter names are the OAuth 2.0 / RFC 7636 wire names, kept verbatim.

## Why

Some identity providers (Google among them) refuse embedded WebViews, so a mobile user signing in with one cannot sign in to the app today. The maintainer ruled option B: reuse better-auth's one-time-token plugin. Triage's first touch on the server card asks for the public surface to be declared in `packages/spec` first.

## Tests

- `src/api/auth-endpoints.test.ts`, a new `mobile sign-in hand-off (one-time token)` block:
  - the two paths are declared and generate is not;
  - the hand-off query is accepted with and without the method;
  - an unknown parameter is refused as `unrecognized_keys`;
  - `plain`, a short challenge, a padded challenge and a missing challenge are refused at their path;
  - the verify body is accepted with the binding (including a verifier with dots and tildes) and refused without it or with a short verifier;
  - the vendor verify body parses.
- `src/system/auth-config.test.ts`: reverse-domain schemes are accepted and the key is absent by default. A table refuses eight shapes at `['trustedAppSchemes', 1]`: `https`, `javascript`, `myapp`, `com.example.app://`, `com.example.app:`, `Com.Example.App`, `com..app` and `com.example.`.
- `src/type-alias-convention.pin.test.ts`: three new `Iso_*` pins and the count.

## Acceptance notes

- No ablation: the diff adds schemas and changes no tested behaviour.

## Verification

All readings below were taken on head `b73cfb24d` (objectstack-ai/objectstack), after the final commit.

- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derived 102 families from the change set (19 paths at derivation, under the 3,000-line threshold). All 102 exit 0. `dispatch-gates --ran` reconciles: 102 run, 0 NOT MEASURED.
- Also run, outside the derivation: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec test` (803 files, 23811 tests passed, 1 todo), `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec typecheck` (exit 0) and `pnpm lint` (exit 0).
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:generated` exit 0: every artifact is current.
- The first pass on `4b54dade` was red on `check:spec-parsed-alias` (the three new aliases needed `Iso_*` pins) and on `check:generated` (declaration map). Both were fixed in this PR. Four gates answered exit 3 (prerequisite: unbuilt packages, or a pinned commit outside the shallow clone) and were then run on the final head after building `formula`, `lint`, `objectql`, `client` and `client-react` and fetching the fixture commit. All four are green there.

<details><summary>Regeneration commands</summary>

`pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:generated --fix` regenerated `api-surface/`, `export-origins/`, `declaration-map/`, `content/docs/references/**` and the strictness-ledger counts. `gen:schema` (via `check:authorable-surface`) wrote `authorable-surface/` and `json-schema.manifest/`. `authorable-surface.base.json` is untouched.

</details>

## Human Minimum

- [x] 1. Schemas start as Zod; `packages/spec` holds no runtime logic.
- [x] 2. Every name I added uses the casing for its kind (the snake_case query keys are the RFC wire names, stated above).
- [x] 3. No formatter ran; `pnpm lint` passes.
- [x] 4. One issue, one branch off an up-to-date `main`, one pull request.
- [x] 5. A change that publishes carries a changeset, and both declaration lines are filled in here and in the changeset.
- [x] 6. `packages/spec` touched: its generated artifacts are regenerated and committed.
- [x] 7. No hand edits to `content/docs/references/`, `packages/*/CHANGELOG.md` or `content/docs/releases/`.
- [x] 8. Title, body and comments are in English.
